entries.title: Judges 16:1
segments:
Gaza; the capital of the southern district of the Philistines. 
 
Many men distinguished by special favors have fallen victims to the blandishments of vicious women, and from their wiles none, without the keeping of God, can be safe.

entries.title: Judges 16:2
segments: No one, when tempted to the commission of sin, can yield to the temptation without exposing himself to be destroyed.

entries.title: Judges 16:3
segments:
Before; in front of. 
 
The punishment of sin is often delayed for a season; but in due time, if men repent not, it will come upon them, and there will be no escape.

entries.title: Judges 16:4
segments:
Sorek; probably near the borders of Dan and the Philistines. 
 
Yielding to temptation increases its power.

entries.title: Judges 16:5
segments:
Eleven hundred pieces of silver; more than two thousand dollars. 
 
Tempters to sin often become tormentors; and those who yield to their enticements, may expect to partake of their plagues.

entries.title: Judges 16:7
segments: The farther men go in transgression, the greater the difficulties of escaping from it; and those who try to deceive others, tempt others to deceive them.

entries.title: Judges 16:9
segments:
In the chamber; in another apartment of the chamber. 
 
God is long-suffering, and often continues his favors to the guilty, not willing that they should perish, but that they should come to repentance.

entries.title: Judges 16:13
segments:
Seven locks; braids or plaits in which his hair may have been arranged. 
 
  Web; the cloth in the loom which Delilah was perhaps weaving.

entries.title: Judges 16:14
segments:
Pin of the beam; rather, pin of the braiding; that is, to which the braided locks with the web were fastened. 
 
Though lying may relieve a man for a moment, yet instead of getting him out of trouble, or in the end benefiting him, it will only plunge him into deeper sorrows.

entries.title: Judges 16:16
segments: Importunity has great influence both with man and with God, and much depends upon resolute, earnest, untiring perseverance.

entries.title: Judges 16:17
segments:
If I be shaven; in losing his hair, he would lose the badge of his Nazariteship and the strength connected with it. 
 
Those who persist in a course of sinning, will soon find themselves weak, helpless, and undone.

entries.title: Judges 16:20
segments: Men without the aid of God, are not aware of their helpless condition till they learn it by experience.

entries.title: Judges 16:21
segments:
Did grind; this was done by turning round a stone with the hands, and was, for a man, a degrading employment. 
 
Those senses which have been the inlets of iniquity often become the organs of punishment.

entries.title: Judges 16:23
segments: The fall of the professed friends of God greatly dishonors him, injures his cause, and gives the wicked occasion to reproach and triumph.

entries.title: Judges 16:25
segments:
Made them sport; was the subject of their sports. 
 
  The pillars; two central pillars near to each other, on which the building mainly rested.

entries.title: Judges 16:27
segments: The triumph of the wicked is short, and the height of their joys is the prelude of their ruin.

entries.title: Judges 16:28
segments: Even the loss of eyesight, great as is the calamity, may be to a man the means of unspeakable good.  If it lead him to repentance of his sins and faith in Jesus Christ, though his grave be with the wicked, his resurrection will be with the just.
